I farm only 6 mu, and I do everything myself, so I will keep the plan simple, steady, and aimed at protecting yield rather than taking chances. Since I have 35 years of experience and well irrigation, I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation on all 6 mu. For wheat, I will use improved seed because it is more dependable for stand and yield than old saved seed, and I will put in moderate fertilizer with nitrogen as the main driver, plus enough phosphorus and potassium to hold the crop steady. Because I have irrigation, I will plan on three waterings for wheat to protect tillering, jointing, and grain filling if the season stays normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what I trust most for stable output on a small farm. I will feed maize a bit more nitrogen than wheat, keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels, and use two irrigations because summer rain helps but I do not want to rely only on rainfall. I will use rotary tillage because it fits my scale, my labor situation, and the way I manage residue between the two crops. I will keep pesticide use limited but not passive: enough applications to control the main disease, weed, and insect pressure, but not so many that I waste money.
